{{Short description|Topological index in chemical graph theory}}
The '''Randić index''', also known as the '''connectivity index''', of a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] is the sum of bond contributions <math>1/(d_i d_j)^{1/2}</math> where <math>d_i</math> and <math>d_j</math> are
the degrees of the vertices making bond&nbsp;''i''&nbsp;~&nbsp;''j''.

==History==
This [[graph invariant]] was introduced by [[Milan Randić]] in 1975.<ref>{{citation|first=M.|last=Randić|authorlink=Milan Randić|title=Characterization of molecular branching|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=97|issue=23|year=1975|pages=6609–6615|doi=10.1021/ja00856a001}}.</ref> It is often used in [[chemoinformatics]] for investigations of [[organic compound]]s.
